newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Opus wins Zimbabwe gaming deal, shares soar.
newsitem.headline: Opus wins Zimbabwe gaming deal, shares soar.

text.p: Games Africa, the parent of Opus Investments Ltd, said on Friday it had won the licence to run "scratchcard" gaming activities in Zimbabwe and that it was well positioned to win the contract to run that country's national lottery.
Opus shares on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange on Friday leapt to their best level in a year on rumours of the firm's success.

Richard Biesheuvel, Games Africa's deputy managing director, told Reuters on Friday it had in fact secured the scratchcard contract almost six months ago but that it had not been announced as he had first wanted to bed down final details of the agreement.
No details on the potential value of the contract were available.

Biesheuvel said Games Africa, which already runs South Africa's scratchcard lottery, may announce shortly a move into other gaming activities here although he ruled out a bid for casino gambling licences which are currently being awarded.
"We are working on other things down here, gaming related things... but not casino licenses. We don't see ourselves in casinos at all, for the moment in any event," Biesheuvel said.

He would not give further details on the group's plans but it has been rumoured that Games Africa is a keen contender for South Africa's national lottery. Biesheuvel said lottery licences were likely to be announced in six to 12 months time.
Opus stocks jumped 27 percent to 950 cents on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange on Friday, bringing its total gains this week to a massive 111 percent.
Volumes on the usually thinly-traded share also picked up with 37,400 stocks traded by 1220 GMT on Friday. Shares had, however, by then slipped off their best levels to 850 cents.
Dealers said there was talk of the share going as high as 20 rand "if all goes according to their plans".

Biesheuvel said bidding for the Zimbabwe lottery would start in about two months time. "Being in there and knowing the market and already having competed our way in there, the probability of us getting the national lottery is better," he said.
He said Games Africa was not bidding for work in other African countries.

Legislation passed last year legalises casino gambling in South Africa for the first time. The National Gambling Act makes provision for the issue of 40 licences and is seen spawning an industry worth an estimated four billion rand a year.
